q01.question: How do I reset my password?
q01.answer:
The process for resetting your password depends on your account type:

* For standard accounts, navigate to Settings, select Security, and then choose Reset Password. You will need to enter your account's email address to receive a reset link, which remains valid for 24 hours. If the link expires, you can request a new one using the same screen.
* If your account is locked due to 5 failed login attempts, you can still request a password reset link during the 15-minute lockout period; using this link will unlock your account immediately.
* If your organization uses Single Sign-On (SSO), the standard reset flow does not apply because your credentials are managed by your organization's identity provider. In this case, you must contact your IT administrator to reset your credentials directly. If SSO is disabled for your organization, users who previously only logged in via SSO will need to use the "forgot password" flow to establish a password for the first time.
contexts:
Go to Settings then Security then Reset Password. Enter the email
address associated with your account and a reset link will be sent.
The link expires 24 hours after it is issued. If it expires, request
a new one from the same screen.

There is no in-app password reset for SSO accounts, because the
password itself is managed entirely by your organization's identity
provider, not by us. If you cannot log in, contact your organization's
IT administrator to reset your credentials in the identity provider
directly. We cannot reset an SSO user's password on our end.

If your organization has enterprise single sign-on enabled, this
consumer password reset flow does not apply to you. See the SSO and
Enterprise Login document for the correct process — resetting a
password here will not affect your SSO login.

After 5 failed login attempts, the account is locked for 15 minutes.
During this window, a password reset link can still be requested and
will unlock the account immediately once used.

Disabling SSO reverts all members to standard email and password
login. Members who never had a password set (because they only ever
logged in via SSO) will need to use the "forgot password" flow once
to set one, exactly like a new consumer account.
q01.ground_truth: Go to Settings, then Security, then Reset Password. Enter your account email and a reset link will be sent; the link expires 24 hours after it's issued.

q02.question: What are the password requirements?
q02.answer: For accounts that utilize standard email and password authentication, passwords must meet a minimum length of 10 characters. Additionally, each password must contain at least one number and one symbol. To ensure security, the system also enforces a history check, meaning a new password cannot match any of the user's previous five passwords.

logged in via SSO) will need to use the "forgot password" flow once
to set one, exactly like a new consumer account.

Organizations on the Enterprise plan can enable single sign-on (SSO)
through an identity provider such as Okta, Azure AD, or Google
Workspace. Once enabled, all members of that organization must log in
through the identity provider's login page — the standard email and
password login screen is disabled for that organization.

password here will not affect your SSO login.
q02.ground_truth: Passwords must be at least 10 characters long and include one number and one symbol. A new password cannot match any of the last 5 passwords used.

q03.answer: If a user makes 5 failed login attempts, their account is automatically locked for a duration of 15 minutes. However, the user is not completely barred from accessing the account during this lockout period; they can still request a password reset link, and using that link will immediately unlock the account.

q04.question: How does SSO login work for enterprise accounts?
q04.answer: For organizations on the Enterprise plan, SSO login functions by routing all members through an external identity provider, such as Okta, Azure AD, or Google Workspace. Once SSO is enabled, the standard email and password login screen is disabled for the entire organization, requiring all members to authenticate via the identity provider's login page instead. Additionally, organizations using enterprise SSO must manage two-factor authentication directly through their chosen identity provider's settings rather than the platform's in-app flow. Furthermore, standard consumer password reset processes do not apply to these accounts; users must follow the specific SSO and Enterprise Login procedures, as resetting a password through the consumer flow will not impact their SSO credentials.

q07.question: How do I set up two-factor authentication?
q07.answer: The method for setting up two-factor authentication (2FA) depends on your organization's plan type. For standard accounts, you can enable 2FA by navigating to Settings, then Security, and selecting Two-Factor Authentication; from there, you must scan the provided QR code using an authenticator app like Google Authenticator or Authy and enter the 6-digit code to confirm the setup. Once enabled, you will be provided with 10 single-use backup codes that should be stored securely in case you lose access to your authenticator app. Conversely, if your organization uses enterprise SSO, you do not use the in-app 2FA flow; instead, 2FA is managed directly through your identity provider's own settings.

q10.question: What is the API rate limit for free tier accounts?
q10.answer: Free tier accounts are subject to specific usage caps to manage API traffic. These accounts are restricted to a maximum of 60 requests per minute and a total of 5,000 requests per day.

q11.question: What happens when I exceed the API rate limit?
q11.answer: When you exceed your API rate limit, the system returns a 429 status code to indicate that the request was unsuccessful. To assist with recovery, the response includes a `Retry-After` header, which specifies the exact number of seconds you must wait before attempting your next request. Additionally, if you continue to receive 429 errors within a short timeframe, the system may impose a temporary IP-level throttle on top of the existing account-level limit.

q16.question: When am I charged for my subscription?
q16.answer:
The timing of your subscription charges depends on the billing frequency of your chosen plan:

* For monthly plans, you are charged on the same calendar day each month as your original signup date [1].
* For annual plans, you are charged once per year on the anniversary of your signup date [1].
* If you choose to upgrade your plan mid-cycle, you will be charged a prorated amount immediately to cover the remainder of your current billing period, followed by the full price of the new plan on your next regular billing date [3].
contexts:
Monthly plans are charged on the same calendar day each month as your
original signup date. Annual plans are charged once per year on the
signup anniversary.

Refunds are available within 14 days of the original charge for any
paid plan. Requests after 14 days are evaluated on a case-by-case
basis and are not guaranteed.

Upgrading mid-cycle charges a prorated amount immediately for the
remainder of the current cycle, then bills the full new plan price on
the next regular billing date.

Go to Billing then Payment History, select the charge, and click
Request Refund. Refunds are processed to the original payment method
within 5-10 business days.

Pro tier customers can request a temporary rate limit increase by
contacting support with their expected peak usage. Increases are
typically approved within one business day.
q16.ground_truth: Monthly plans are charged on the same calendar day each month as the original signup date. Annual plans are charged once per year on the signup anniversary.
